AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To determine native individual bilateral differences in femoral version in a diverse population.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Computed tomography scans with complete imaging of uninjured bilateral femora were used to determine femoral version and individual bilateral differences in version. Age, sex, and ethnicity of each subject were also collected. Femoral version and individual bilateral differences in version were correlated with demographic variables using univariate and multivariate regression models.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: 164 subjects were included in the study. The average femoral version was 9.4° (± 9.4°). The mean individual bilateral difference in femoral version was 5.4° (± 4.4°, p < 0.001). 17.7% of subjects had a difference in version ≥10° and 4.3% had a difference in version ≥15°. A femur with anteversion ≥20° or retroversion was associated with a greater mean difference in version from the contralateral side compared to those with mid-range anteversion.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Bilateral differences in femoral version are common and can result in a difference from native anatomy that may be clinically significant if only the contralateral limb is used to establish rotational alignment during intramedullary stabilization of diaphyseal femur fractures. This is also an important consideration when considering malrotation of femur fractures since most studies define malrotation as a greater than 10-15° difference compared to the contralateral side.
